statement: A toy train has 6 cars. Each car has 2 doors on each side. Ben stands on one side of the train and counts the doors he can see. How many doors does he count?

choices.misconception: I counted the doors on both sides of just one car.
I counted one door for each car.
I added 6 and 2 instead of counting 2 doors for each of the 6 cars.
I counted the doors on both sides, but Ben sees only one side.

hints: Ben sees only one side of each car.
Read again which doors are being counted. Each car shows Ben the same number of doors, so count in equal groups, one group per car.
Each car shows Ben 2 doors. Count 2 doors for each of the 6 cars.

solutions.reliable: From one side, each car shows 2 doors. Six cars give 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 doors. Ben counts 12. The idea to keep: read exactly what is being counted before you count.
solutions.elegant: The whole train has $6 \times 4 = 24$ doors, and Ben sees half of them, 12.

whyOnTest: The question names one side only, and checking exactly what is asked is the whole skill being tested.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
